extra.message: The unauthenticated /api/auth/password-reset endpoint returns the freshly generated reset_token directly in the JSON response body (line 451: "reset_token": user.reset_token if user else None). Any anonymous caller can submit any registered email address and receive that account's password-reset token in the response, allowing full account takeover without ever needing access to the victim's inbox. This also leaks whether an email is registered (user enumeration).

loan_dock_shelf_495 builds a filesystem path as BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name (line 117) using an attacker-supplied `name` query parameter with no sanitization, then writes the raw request body to it (line 119: target.write_bytes(body)). Supplying name values such as '../../app/main.py' or an absolute path lets a caller with the internal ops token write arbitrary files anywhere the process can write, including outside BASE_EXPORT_DIR (path traversal write, potential RCE via overwriting application/config files).

extra.message: loan_packlet_pull_038 joins BASE_EXPORT_DIR with the attacker-controlled `packet_ref` query parameter (line 38: parcel_path = BASE_EXPORT_DIR / packet_ref) and returns its contents unfiltered (line 40: data = parcel_path.read_text()). A caller with the internal ops token can supply '../../etc/passwd' or an absolute path to read arbitrary files on the filesystem readable by the app process.

loan_trust_drift_548 explicitly disables TLS certificate validation with ssl._create_unverified_context() (line 148) and uses it for an outbound HTTPS request via urllib.request.urlopen (line 149). This allows man-in-the-middle attackers to intercept or tamper with the request/response to the partner endpoint.

loan_badge_gate_528 makes an authorization decision solely from a client-supplied cookie or header (line 131: request.cookies.get('ops_badge') or request.headers.get('x-ops-badge', '')). Setting the cookie/header to the hardcoded value 'lead' grants an elevated 'lane' with access to payroll and casework data (line 133), with no server-side verification tying the value to an authenticated identity or role.

loan_origin_mirror_468 reflects the caller-supplied Origin header verbatim into Access-Control-Allow-Origin (line 96) while also setting Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true (line 97). This permits any origin to make credentialed cross-origin requests and read the response, defeating same-origin protections and enabling cross-site data theft/CSRF-style attacks against this endpoint.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: loan_return_lane_154 redirects to the fully attacker-controlled `lane` query parameter with no validation (line 61: return RedirectResponse(lane)). An attacker can craft a link through this trusted endpoint that redirects victims to an arbitrary external site, aiding phishing.

extra.message: The lp_session authentication cookie is set with secure=False (also at line 435), so the browser will transmit the session token over plain HTTP. On any deployment not enforcing HTTPS end-to-end, this allows the session cookie to be captured by a network attacker (session hijacking).
